\section{Experimental design}
\label{sec:design}
We partnered with a large employer and randomized 1,150 newly hired employees into a control group and a treatment group with automatic enrollment at a 3\% contribution rate. The experiment was preregistered. Participants also completed an online survey programmed in oTree, in which they made incentivized intertemporal choices.\footnote{Payments were made through the employer's payroll system within two weeks.}

In the survey, participants were told that their choices would be matched with a real coworker, although all partners were simulated by the computer. We ran 12 survey sessions between March and May 2025.

Let $\beta$ denote the present-bias parameter and $\delta$ the long-run discount factor. The utility of a consumption stream is
\begin{equation}
U_t = u(c_t) + \beta \sum_{k=1}^{T} \delta^k u(c_{t+k}).
\label{eq:qh}
\end{equation}
Equation~\eqref{eq:qh} reduces to exponential discounting when $\beta = 1$.

The mean rating of plan clarity was 3.47 on a five-point scale ($N = 25$ pilot participants).
